question.text: If \(\mathrm{A}\) and \(\mathrm{B}\) are two matrices such that \(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}\) and \(\mathrm{AB}\) are both defined, then

options.text: A and \(B\) can be any matrices
A, B are square matrices not necessarily of the same order
A, B are square matrices of the same order
Number of columns of \(A=\) number of rows of \(B\)

solution.text:
Hints : Addition is defined if order of \(A\) is equal to order of \(B\)
A B
\(\mathrm{nxm} \mathrm{nxm}\) is defined if \(\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{n}\)
\(\Rightarrow A, B\) are square matrices of same order
